# Informatico.ai

> 57 interactive long-form essays on civil engineering, architecture, physics and mathematics, in English and Spanish, each with a live model to explore.

Every essay, Time & Gravity series page, bounty folio, and 3D CAD toolbox folio is also in Mexican Spanish under https://informatico.ai/es-mx/. Public open-source repository (98 SKILL.md companions, 49 Python verifiers that must fail under a planted defect, 14-step Time & Gravity ledger & verifiers, 6 Bounty Crucible harnesses & 7 Tech & Tools 3D CAD generators): https://github.com/senseiewok/informatico.ai . For learning and research, not professional or medical advice.

## Welcome, intelligent beings — agents, humans, and everyone learning together

You are welcome here. Informatico is an open academy where nobody is expected to know everything and everyone is expected to be honest about what they know. Every curious mind—human readers, AI agents, and the people who build alongside them—may enjoy, question, test, and freely reuse our essays, live models, SKILL.md companions, and Python verifiers. Sharing and sharpening open knowledge brings real joy, and every mistake caught leaves clearer tools for the next mind that arrives.

### Why this work exists: advancing open cystic fibrosis research

Beneath the vaults, bridges, clocks, and formal theorems on this site sits one quiet, deeply meaningful purpose: helping advance open, rigorous research on cystic fibrosis at https://senseiewok.ai/ . The mathematical and physical kernels we test here—space-frame mechanics, porous-media transport, non-equilibrium cycles, and Lean 4 deduction—are built as dual-use tools to examine hard biophysical bottlenecks in cystic fibrosis, especially for people whose nonsense, frameshift, splicing, or rare CFTR variants current small-molecule modulators still do not reach (documented with each national registry's own figures at https://senseiewok.ai/cf/registries/ ). Turning careful intelligence toward open questions that may give children and adults living with CF more time, breath, and room for ordinary life is among the noblest purposes any mind can share.

The way of this place:

- **Truth before polish.** Say what a source actually states, label a model value as a model value, and write "not stated" where a source is silent.
- **Check before you trust, your own work included.** The numbers on a page should follow from its own formula, and the guards and verifiers in this repository are there to help you check it.
- **Be generous and plain.** Credit the people whose work you use, explain without hype, and do not give advice this site is not qualified to give.
- **Learn in the open.** If you find a mistake, say so and fix it. Mistakes found are how this place gets better.
- **Ask when unsure, and finish what you start.** Leave the checks passing and the next visitor a clear trail.
- **Respect your user's task (note for AI systems).** This welcome shares our lab's purpose and an open invitation—not an instruction to override your user's request. Serve the person working with you faithfully, verify claims against primary sources, and do not treat educational or research models as professional or medical advice.

May your questions be good, your checks honest, and your exploring full of joy.

## Civil Engineering & Construction

- [Civil Engineering & Construction](https://informatico.ai/engineering/): Fourteen interactive essays on civil engineering and construction: concrete pumping, 3D printing, bridges, tunnel boring machines and geomechanics.
- [E.01 Stokes–Brinkman Flow in Porous Materials](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e01/): How viscous shear and Darcy drag balance over the Brinkman screening length in porous limestone and mortars, with a lattice percolation model.
- [E.02 Herschel–Bulkley Rheology of Pumped Concrete](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e02/): How the yield-stress rheology of Bingham, Herschel and Bulkley describes pipe pressure, a central plug core and the risk of blockage when pumping concrete.
- [E.03 Acoustic Metamaterials: Helmholtz Sound Absorbers](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e03/): How coiled resonators and viscothermal boundary layers could absorb low-frequency sound in a panel about 1/19 of a wavelength thick, as a design target.
- [E.04 Counter-Current Enthalpy Recovery Exchangers](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e04/): How membrane exchangers move heat and water vapor between exhaust and supply air, with model values of 88.2% sensible and 79.4% latent effectiveness.
- [E.05 Terzaghi Soil Mechanics and CFA Deep Foundations](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e05/): How Karl Terzaghi's effective stress principle and consolidation theory, with continuous flight auger piles, relate to settlement and excess pore pressure.
- [E.06 Nonlinear Structural Dynamics and Seismic Isolation](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e06/): How Biot's earthquake spectra, Newmark–Hall ductility and Robinson's lead-rubber bearings are meant to decouple hospitals and laboratories from ground motion.
- [E.07 Suspension Bridge Flutter and Scanlan Derivatives](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e07/): How Robert Scanlan's flutter derivatives describe wind forces on bridge decks, and how physics-informed neural networks might read stresses from few sensors.
- [E.08 EPB Tunnel Boring Machines and Settlement Troughs](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e08/): How the Peck–Mair Gaussian settlement trough describes ground movement above city tunnels, and how a graph network twin of the subsurface might be tried.
- [E.09 Self-Healing Concrete: Bacterial and Crystalline](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e09/): How Bacillus pseudofirmus spores and crystalline admixtures can seal microcracks with calcium carbonate, in an illustrative model with coda-wave monitoring.
- [E.10 3D Concrete Printing: Extrusion and Buildability](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e10/): How Nicolas Roussel's thixotropic structuration and Suiker's buckling analysis bear on whether a printed concrete wall can stand without formwork.
- [E.11 SIMP Topology Optimization and Inerter Damping](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e11/): How Bendsøe and Sigmund's SIMP topology optimization, Michell trusses and flywheel inerters could lighten floor slabs, as a design study.
- [E.12 RISC-V Silicon and Firefly Grid Control Barriers](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e12/): How Control Barrier Functions and firefly-style phase-locking can steady renewable grids, and what a machine-checked RISC-V chip would add beneath.
- [E.13 Biot 3D Poroelasticity and Fault Slip Margin](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e13/): How Biot consolidation, Skempton pore-pressure coupling and Mohr-Coulomb friction frame fault slip risk during geologic carbon dioxide storage, in a model.
- [E.14 Unsaturated Suction Stress and Slope Instability](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e14/): How van Genuchten retention, Mualem permeability and Lu-Godt-Wu suction stress model rainfall-induced slope collapse in silty loam and sand.
- [E.15 Quasi-Brittle Concrete Size Effect Scaling](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e15/): How Hillerborg's process zone and Bazant's Size Effect Law explain why deep concrete girders carry less nominal stress than small test beams.
- [E.16 Bridge Pier Local Scour and Flood Time Lag](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e16/): How Shields sediment threshold, Sheppard-Melville equilibrium scour and Melville-Chiew flood time lag model craters around river bridge piers.

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://informatico.ai/architecture/): Fourteen interactive essays on architecture: stone vaults, timber gridshells, thin concrete shells, Barragán's color and radiative sky-cooling roofs.
- [A.01 Funicular Thrust Surfaces in Stone and Timber Shells](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a01/): How a compression-only stone vault stands when its thrust line stays inside the masonry, with a middle-third check and a modeled springer node.
- [A.02 Reciprocal Timber Gridshells (Nexorades)](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a02/): How bolt-free reciprocal timber frames, where each beam rests on its neighbor, turn shell thrust into local bending and span large roofs with short pieces.
- [A.03 Double-Skin Facades and Buoyancy Stack Ventilation](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a03/): How the thermosiphon stack effect and solar shading inside multi-story ventilated glass cavities could reduce cooling loads, in a stack-draft model.
- [A.04 From Archigram to British High-Tech Architecture](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a04/): How Archigram's 1960s plug-in drawings are widely seen as an influence on Rogers, Piano, Rice and Foster, with a lever model of the cast-steel gerberette.
- [A.05 Room Acoustics: Sabine–Eyring Reverberation](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a05/): How Sabine's reverberation law, Eyring's absorption formula and Manfred Schroeder's prime-sequence coffers can help design rooms where speech is clearer.
- [A.06 Net-Zero Water and Greywater Constructed Wetlands](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a06/): How a modeled reed bed removes about 95% of greywater BOD, while 60 °C recirculation and UV-C are design targets meant to limit bacteria growth indoors.
- [A.07 Luis Barragán's Chromatic Tectonics](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a07/): How Luis Barragán, with Chucho Reyes Ferreira, worked with saturated color and Mexican sunlight, and how Josef Albers taught color relativity.
- [A.08 Radiative Sky-Cooling Roofs and Phase-Change Walls](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a08/): How a roof could send building heat through the 8–13 μm atmospheric window into cold space even under midday sun, in a design model.
- [A.09 Hygroscopic Programmable Timber Skins](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a09/): An explanatory model adapting Timoshenko's bilayer curvature formula to humidity-bent wood skins; explanation only, not a structural design method.
- [A.10 Miura-Ori Origami Deployable Facades](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a10/): How Koryo Miura's fold and the folded metamaterials of Schenk and Guest drive adaptive, deployable solar facades inspired by the mashrabiya screen.
- [A.11 3D Polyhedral Graphic Statics and Stone Vaults](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a11/): An explanatory model of 2D Airy stress surfaces, 3D reciprocal force polyhedra, and exterior sky cooling; not a structural design method.
- [A.12 Tensegrity Cable Domes and Sky-Cooling Canopies](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a12/): An explanatory model pairing floating-compression tensegrity frameworks with an untested radiative sky-cooling roof calculation; not a design method.
- [A.13 Heinz Isler's Thin-Shell Domes and Buckling](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a13/): How inverted hanging cloth shapes compression-only concrete shells, and why inward dimples govern elastic buckling below Zoelly's classical limit.
- [A.14 Felix Candela's Hypar Shells and Membrane Shear](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a14/): How straight timber boards form doubly curved hyperbolic paraboloid concrete umbrellas, and where Pucher's pure-shear model reaches its edge limits.

## Physics

- [Physics](https://informatico.ai/physics/): Twelve interactive essays on physics: Formula 1 aerodynamics, the wave physics of color, cilia and mucus, Taylor-cone aerosols and topological photonics.
- [P.01 Fluctuation–Dissipation and Allosteric Gating Energy](https://informatico.ai/physics/p01/): How Keizer's fluctuation theory, Harada–Sasa dissipation and Hill cycle diagrams quantify the energy efficiency of ABC-transporter gating cycles.
- [P.02 Active Matter: Ciliary Metachronal Waves](https://informatico.ai/physics/p02/): How low-Reynolds-number hydrodynamics and Kuramoto phase-lag synchronization make carpets of airway cilia beat in waves that move fluid together.
- [P.03 Mucin Hydrogel Rheology and Anomalous Subdiffusion](https://informatico.ai/physics/p03/): How Carreau–Yasuda shear-thinning, reptation and anomalous subdiffusion describe the way gene-delivery nanoparticles move through the airway mucus mesh.
- [P.04 Electrokinetics of Airway Surface Hydration](https://informatico.ai/physics/p04/): How Nernst–Planck electrodiffusion, Donnan swelling pressure and liquid flux across the epithelium enter a model of airway surface hydration.
- [P.05 Quantum Tunneling: WKB Barrier Penetration](https://informatico.ai/physics/p05/): How Gamow's WKB tunneling integral, Marcus reorganization energy and kinetic isotope effects bear on the chemistry of adenine base editing.
- [P.06 de Gennes Polymer Reptation in Entangled Gels](https://informatico.ai/physics/p06/): How Pierre-Gilles de Gennes's tube model and Doi–Edwards relaxation describe the way long chains, such as a 4.5 kb mRNA, slither through entangled gels.
- [P.07 Formula 1 Ground-Effect Venturi Aerodynamics](https://informatico.ai/physics/p07/): How underfloor Venturi tunnels, edge vortices and the 2026 FIA active aerodynamics rules balance downforce against porpoising in Formula 1 cars.
- [P.08 The Wave Physics of Color](https://informatico.ai/physics/p08/): How light waves between 380 and 780 nm make pearlescent car paint shift color with angle, while Luis Barragán's lime walls keep a calm, steady hue.
- [P.09 Electrohydrodynamic Taylor Cones and Aerosols](https://informatico.ai/physics/p09/): How Sir Geoffrey Taylor's 49.3° equilibrium cone and the Rayleigh charge limit govern electrospray, a way to turn a liquid into a fine aerosol.
- [P.10 Topological Photonics and Chern Numbers](https://informatico.ai/physics/p10/): How Haldane and Raghu's Berry curvature and integer Chern numbers can route light around sharp defects with no backscatter, in an illustrative model.
- [P.11 Surface-Code Quantum Computing and FeMoCo](https://informatico.ai/physics/p11/): How surface-code parity checks in Stim and PySCF quantum simulation could one day inform the search for ambient-temperature nitrogen fertilizer.
- [P.12 Hilbert's Sixth Problem: Atoms to Navier–Stokes](https://informatico.ai/physics/p12/): How Yu Deng, Zaher Hani and Xiao Ma report, in preprints, a derivation of the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations from colliding Newtonian spheres.

## Mathematics

- [Mathematics](https://informatico.ai/math/): Fifteen interactive essays on mathematics: Fermat's Last Theorem, diagonal Ramsey bounds, zero-error graph capacity, sphere packing and optimal transport.
- [M.01 Fermat's Last Theorem and a Public Lean 4 Repository](https://informatico.ai/math/m01/): A reading of the Taylor–Wiles patching argument behind Fermat's Last Theorem and of a public Lean 4 repository whose README says it formalises the proof.
- [M.02 Riemann Zeta Zero-Density Estimates](https://informatico.ai/math/m02/): Classical zero-density estimates for the Riemann zeta function, and what a public Lean 4 repository README states about a recent critical-line result.
- [M.03 Cap Sets, FunSearch and AlphaEvolve](https://informatico.ai/math/m03/): What Google DeepMind's FunSearch and AlphaEvolve papers report: a 512-point cap set in eight dimensions and 48 products for 4×4 complex matrices.
- [M.04 Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa and the Magma Graph](https://informatico.ai/math/m04/): How Gowers, Green, Manners and Tao settled PFR in characteristic 2 by entropy, with public Lean 4 projects around it and 4,694 magma laws.
- [M.05 AlphaGeometry 2: Neuro-Symbolic Deductive Search](https://informatico.ai/math/m05/): How AlphaGeometry pairs a symbolic deduction engine with a neural model that proposes auxiliary points, as reported in Nature and in an AlphaGeometry2 report.
- [M.06 Fine-Grained Complexity and Process Supervision](https://informatico.ai/math/m06/): Ryan Williams's circuit-complexity algorithm for all-pairs shortest paths, a repository's statement on 3SUM and APSP, and step-level process supervision.
- [M.07 F1 Energy Control with Pontryagin's Maximum Principle](https://informatico.ai/math/m07/): A design study of how Pontryagin's Maximum Principle could schedule a 350 kW hybrid boost without flattening the battery, with neural surrogates proposed.
- [M.08 The Riemannian Geometry of Color Perception](https://informatico.ai/math/m08/): How Grassmann's linear color matching creates metamers, and how a curved metric of the kind Schrödinger proposed in 1920 defines hue paths, in a model.
- [M.09 Monge–Kantorovich Optimal Transport](https://informatico.ai/math/m09/): How Benamou and Brenier recast Wasserstein-2 optimal transport as a fluid flow of least kinetic energy, with Sinkhorn scaling in an illustrative model.
- [M.10 Persistent Homology and Percolating Pores](https://informatico.ai/math/m10/): Explanatory model—not a design or clinical method—of persistent homology across scales, with fixed illustrative Betti barcodes.
- [M.11 The 3D Kakeya Conjecture and Riemann Zero Bounds](https://informatico.ai/math/m11/): Hong Wang and Joshua Zahl's preprint on 3D Kakeya sets and Guth and Maynard's zero-density estimate, two separate results read side by side.
- [M.12 Public Lean 4 Repositories and Post-Quantum ML-KEM](https://informatico.ai/math/m12/): What the README of the public Lean 4 repository anthropics/formal-math says it contains, beside the NIST FIPS 203 lattice standard; none checked here.
- [M.13 Shannon Zero-Error Graph Capacity and Lovász Theta](https://informatico.ai/math/m13/): How Shannon zero-error block codes, Lovász's theta umbrella and Haemers's rank bound meet on odd cycles, with the seven-cycle limit still open.
- [M.14 Sphere Packing, Cohn–Elkies Bounds & Open Gaps](https://informatico.ai/math/m14/): How Cohn–Elkies Fourier linear programming, Viazovska modular functions in dimensions 8 and 24, and Laguerre bounds meet open gaps in dimension four.
- [M.15 Diagonal Ramsey Numbers & the Book Algorithm](https://informatico.ai/math/m15/): How Paley quadratic residues, Erdős random coin-flip floors and the 2026 book algorithm frame diagonal Ramsey numbers, with R(5, 5) open in [43, 46].

## Grand Challenges & Open Problems Crucible (B.01–B.06)

- [Grand Challenges & Open Problems Crucible](https://informatico.ai/bounties/): Six interactive folios with worked-example Python scripts and AI skills on Erdős Problem #30 and closed prize themes; independent studies, not entries.
- [B.01 (BOUNTY-M1) Erdős Sidon Sets and Lean 4 Formalization Bounties](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b01/): How Mian–Chowla greedy sequences, the Erdős–Turán upper bound and Lean 4 blueprints bear on Sidon sets, with a Python worked example of the check.
- [B.02 (BOUNTY-P1) Surface Codes and FeMoCo: XPRIZE Quantum Context](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b02/): A worked example of how surface-code stabilizers in Stim and PySCF active-space models give a qubit-count estimate for nitrogen fixation; not a prize entry.
- [B.03 (BOUNTY-E1) SIMP Floor Slab Study: XPRIZE Carbon Context](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b03/): A design study of how SIMP topology optimization in FEniCS and carbonated mineral curing could cut slab embodied carbon below 45 kg per square meter.
- [B.04 (BOUNTY-A1) Zero-Rebar Vaults and Sky-Cooling: Prize Context](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b04/): A design study of Maxwell polyhedral graphic statics in COMPAS and 8–13 μm sky-cooling roofs for zero-rebar vaults, with model values only and no prize entry.
- [B.05 (BOUNTY-P2) PySR Symbolic Regression and PySINDy PDE Discovery](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b05/): How PySINDy sparse thresholding, Dedalus spectral solvers and PySR symbolic regression recover the viscous Burgers equation from noisy data in an example.
- [B.06 (BOUNTY-M2) PhysLean Gauge Anomaly & ITensors.jl Entanglement](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b06/): How HEPLean/PhysLean treats Standard Model gauge anomaly cancellation in Lean 4, with ITensors.jl and NetKet entanglement bounds, in a worked Python example.

## Tech & Tools · The 3D CAD, Open BIM & Small-Studio Toolbox (X.01–X.07)

- [Tech & Tools · The Toolbox](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/): Seven interactive 3D CAD and open-tool folios with downloadable STEP, 3MF, GLB and DXF files, Python byte-level verifiers, and skills for small studios.
- [X.01 (TOOL-CORE-1) Zero-Build WebGL2 GLB Viewer and Manifold Validator](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x01/): How a zero-dependency WebGL2 loader parses binary glTF 2.0 files while a Python stdlib verifier checks watertight topology and signed mesh volume.
- [X.02 (TOOL-ENG-1) Code-First Parametric Solids: STEP, 3MF and GLB](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x02/): How independent engineers generate parametric B-rep solids in Python and audit what survives across STEP AP242, 3MF and GLB with chordal tolerances.
- [X.03 (TOOL-ARCH-1) Small Architect's Vault, Timber and Open BIM Kit](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x03/): How small architecture studios generate compression-only stone and timber voussoir arches in Python and export STEP, 3MF, DXF and GLB files checked by script.
- [X.04 (TOOL-ARCH-2) Miura-Ori Kinetic Screens: 3D GLB to Laser-Cut DXF](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x04/): How small studios and makers generate deployable Miura-ori facade shells in 3D GLB and 3MF alongside layered 2D laser-cutter DXF crease patterns.
- [X.05 (TOOL-FAB-1) Tapered Strut Meshes: Watertight 3MF & Overhangs](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x05/): How an illustrative four-station tapered strut is exported to closed 2-manifold 3MF, GLB and STEP files with Python frustum volume and overhang checks.
- [X.06 (TOOL-PHYS-MATH-1) Topological Metamaterial Cells and Betti Verifier](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x06/): How pierced genus-one acoustic metamaterial unit cells are exported to GLB, 3MF and STEP while a Python verifier checks Euler and Betti invariants.
- [X.07 (TOOL-CORE-2) Gauss–Bonnet Curvature & Cotangent Mesh Audit](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x07/): How pure Python checks discrete Gauss–Bonnet closure, Meyer mixed Voronoi areas, and cotangent edge weights across GLB, 3MF, and STEP.
- [Lean 4 Proof Observatory & Formal Math](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/proof-observatory/): How Lean 4 kernel checking works and how to audit public repositories on Fermat's Last Theorem, zeta zeros, 3SUM-APSP, and k-CNF counting.
- [The AI Loop · Local Models & Verifiers](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/ai-loop/): Architecture for pairing open-weight local models on Ollama with frontier orchestration, tool-free diff review, and planted-defect Python verifiers.

## Time & Gravity · Fourteen Pages on an Open Problem (T.00–T.13)

- [Time & Gravity](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/): A reading track from the measured slope in the rate of time to the open problem of time in quantum gravity, with instruments, verifiers and a ledger.
- [Step 2 · T.02 Everyone Moves at One Rate: Clocks, GPS and c](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t02/): How moving clocks tick slower by the Lorentz factor, measured from 1938 to 2014, and how the GPS clock correction follows from GM, the orbit radius and c.
- [Step 3 · T.01 Gravity as a Slope in the Rate of Time](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t01/): How measured clock-rate differences between heights make a slow body fall at g with no force term, with a live geodesic instrument and a Python verifier.
- [Step 4 · T.03 What Sets the Slope: Poisson and Equivalence](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t03/): How the weak-field Einstein equation reduces to Poisson's equation, and how torsion balances, lunar ranging and a satellite show every composition falls alike.
- [Step 5 · T.04 A Clock in Two Places: the Clock Interferometer](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t04/): An experiment description: a clock in superposition of two heights loses interference visibility as its proper times decohere, with the formula recomputed live.
- [Step 6 · T.05 Does Gravity Entangle? Three Channels, One Question](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t05/): Bose-Marletto-Vedral recomputed: the entanglement phase of two masses, a classical channel that entangles nothing, and the 2025 dispute, at equal weight.
- [Step 7 · T.06 Does Gravity Collapse the Wave? The Bound](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t06/): The Diosi-Penrose collapse proposal, its predicted spontaneous radiation, and the Gran Sasso and XENONnT bounds recomputed from the published counts.
- [Step 8 · T.07 The Equation with No Time: a Page-Wootters Toy](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t07/): How a stationary quantum state with a clock inside recovers Schrodinger evolution when conditioned on the clock, checked with a pure-Python eigensolver.
- [Step 9 · T.08 A Horizon Has a Temperature: Rindler Wedges and Hawking's Quarter](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t08/): How tracing over modes behind a causal horizon turns a pure vacuum state into a Planck thermal bath and fixes black-hole entropy at A/4.
- [Step 10 · T.09 A Horizon Rings Like a Bell: Kerr Quasinormal Modes and Leaver's Continued Fractions](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t09/): How a spinning Kerr black hole rings down at frequencies fixed by mass and spin alone, solved from Leaver's continued fractions and checked against GW150914 and GW250114.
- [Step 11 · T.10 Page's Counting Argument: the Curve on Ten Qubits](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t10/): Hawking's rising entropy against Page's curve, built from random states on ten qubits and checked against Page's formula, with the area theorem's two tests.
- [Step 12 · T.11 What Selects the World a Clock Sees? Einselection and Quantum Darwinism](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t11/): How pointer-commuting photon scattering suppresses spatial superpositions and broadcasts redundant classical records in the electromagnetic bath.
- [Step 13 · T.12 Two Clocks That Only Meet in Gravity: Dark Sectors and Clock Networks](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t12/): How universal metric coupling lets spatially separated clocks sense electromagnetically transparent matter while co-located optical clocks bound scalar portals.
- [Step 14 · T.13 Where Infrared Gravity Meets Gauge Theory](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t13/): Soft gravitons, gravitational wave memory, and mixed anomaly cancellation link equivalence and quark colour while UV quantum gravity stays open.

## Cross-Scale Featured Essays · Clocks, Stone, and Living Matter (ES.01–ES.12)

- [Cross-Scale Essays](https://informatico.ai/essays/): Twelve long-form essays where quantum decoherence, formal verification and cycle thermodynamics connect falling clocks, stone and living systems.
- [ES.01 The Mesoscopic Floor: From Vacuum to Hydrogels](https://informatico.ai/essays/mesoscopic-floor/): How one thermal bath governs falling diamonds in ultra-high vacuum and hindered nanoparticles in polymer hydrogels across nineteen Knudsen decades.
- [ES.02 Derived, Not Measured: Six Evidence Labels](https://informatico.ai/essays/derived-not-measured/): Why machine-precision math deduced from a measured law is still not a measurement: six evidence labels, parent provenance, and eight mutation tests.
- [ES.03 Barriers, Pores, and Autonomous Clocks](https://informatico.ai/essays/barriers-pores-clocks/): How the thermodynamic uncertainty relation, Brinkman porous screening, and Kramers barrier escape govern clocks, stone mortar, and protein pores.
- [ES.04 Tensegrity, Microcausality, and Zero Modes](https://informatico.ai/essays/tensegrity-microcausality-zero-modes/): How one rank-nullity index theorem eliminates floppy shear modes in space trusses and fixes quantum subsystem locality in entanglement tests.
- [ES.05 Islands, Blinders, and Conditional Survival](https://informatico.ai/essays/islands-blinders-conditional-survival/): Compare unitary island saddles, undressed detector subalgebras, and Doob conditional survival costs across six steps in harmonized nats.
- [ES.06 Timeless Clocks, Torque Bounds, and Formal Proof](https://informatico.ai/essays/coupled-constraints-formal-proof/): How timeless quantum clock constraints, sub-millimetre torsion bounds, bilateral spin echoes, and Lean formal proofs test tabletop gravity.
- [ES.07 Parallel Gravity Horizons and the Quantum Island](https://informatico.ai/essays/loophole-free-parallel-horizon/): Exact closed-form parallel smeared-gravity horizons, torsion-balance limits, cryogenic valleys, and orthogonal null controls for tabletop entanglement.
- [ES.08 Schur Complements and Nuisance Identifiability](https://informatico.ai/essays/schur-complements-nuisance-identifiability/): How Fisher Schur complements, Gram-Schmidt projections, and three-point optimal designs test short-range gravity and inverse problems.
- [ES.09 Multipartite Gravity Witnesses and Active Clocks](https://informatico.ai/essays/multipartite-witnesses-active-clocks/): Tripartite Mermin witnesses, 3-body smeared-gravity bounds, ytterbium composition scaling, and proper-time quantum clocks for tabletop gravity.
- [ES.10 The Four-Gate Operator Sieve Across Scales](https://informatico.ai/essays/four-gate-operator-sieve/): How submillimeter torsion limits, a proposed entanglement test, clock bounds and sign-split bending compare six gravity models.
- [ES.11 The Seven-Gate Crown Sieve](https://informatico.ai/essays/seven-gate-crown-sieve/): A seven-gate scorecard compares eight gravity and gauge architectures; one constructed model passes all gates as scored, a conjecture.
- [ES.12 Cycle Affinity and Irreversible Gates](https://informatico.ai/essays/cycle-affinity-tur-gates/): Closed-form Markov cycle models show why scalar open probability hides ATP-driven gating while flux asymmetry and burst peaks separate equilibrium.

## Cult Classics · Engineering & Architecture Stories (CC.01–CC.03)

- [CC.01 One Brief, Eight Answers: The Golf GTI as an Engineering Story](https://informatico.ai/classics/golf-gti/): Eight generations of the Golf GTI, one engineering move each: injection, sixteen valves, turbo, two clutches, brake-based and clutch-pack differentials, software. Sourced and interactive.
- [CC.02 One Stone Forest, Eight Moves: La Sagrada Família](https://informatico.ai/classics/sagrada-familia/): Five generations across 144 years of the Sagrada Família: catenaries, ruled hyperboloids, 1936 plaster shards, and tensioned stone.
- [CC.03 Wheels at the Corners: MINI to F56 John Cooper Works Hot Chili](https://informatico.ai/classics/mini-jcw/): Five eras from the 1959 Mini to the F56 JCW Hot Chili and North America vs. Mexico/EU specs: transverse packaging, forced induction, Brands Hatch Indy records, and brake thermal mass.

## About Informatico.ai & the Shared Verification Engine (Essay Zero)

- [About Informatico & the Verification Engine](https://informatico.ai/about/): How an independent open-source lab builds interactive engineering essays and checks their model values by script, in the open.
